# I ❤️ PY

> A demo app about producing high-quality Python, written entirely in
> Python, that proves its own production quality via live tool output
> rather than asserting it.

## Docs
- [docs/spec.md](./docs/spec.md): full specification — modules, repo structure, open questions, and the list of specified-but-not-shipped gaps
- [MANIFEST.md](./MANIFEST.md): application-level intent, per the Otrobonita playbook convention
- [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md): standing instructions for coding agents — pure-Python constraint, commit discipline, architecture
- [README.md](./README.md): human-facing overview, quickstart, reusable parts
- [generated/docs/wiring-diagram.html](./generated/docs/wiring-diagram.html): the five tabs wired to their real tools — generated HTML, open in a browser

## Run it
```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\activate    # Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .[dev]
python app.py                                      # http://localhost:8321
pytest --cov                                       # quality stack; coverage floor is a real gate
```

## API (running app)
- `GET /api/health` — liveness probe. Returns `{"ok": "true", "service": "i-love-python", "heart": "real"}`
- `GET /api/telemetry` — full `TelemetryReport` JSON: every quality tool's real output, verdict, and duration. This is the data behind the Quality tab.

## Constraints
- All source is Python. Non-Python artifacts (the k6 script, CI YAML, pre-commit hook, wiring diagram) are generated by Python in this repo, never hand-authored — see docs/spec.md §0 and §6.
- No fakes: anything displayed must come from a real tool run, a real git command, or a clearly-labelled simulator/fixture. The same standard applies to what an agent reports back to a human — measure it, don't infer it.

## About the Pure Python Rule

The rule is, first and foremost, a discipline exercise — a way of holding a single mental model and a unified toolchain across the entire repo. But it also has a forward-looking angle: if AI orchestration (agent loops, tool selection, RAG) keeps shifting the center of gravity in web apps from interface to model infrastructure, that infrastructure already lives in Python. This isn't a claim that it will happen — just a scenario in which the choice would already turn out to have been right, rather than a retrofitted justification.

We also plan to measure how agents perform when working in a single language, compared to task-switching between languages and formats — and the context-window cost of loading rules from multiple frameworks at once.
